display.title: Simchas Beis Hashoeva Night 6: The Rebbe Maharash and the Innkeeper's Trial
display.summary_short: On the night of the Rebbe Maharash, a live Sukkos rally teaches Lechatchila Ariber and tells how the Rebbe's puzzling delay saved a falsely accused innkeeper.
display.summary_long: Recorded live at a Simchas Beis Hashoeva rally for children during Chol HaMoed Sukkos 5786, on the night of the Rebbe Maharash and his motto 'Lechatchila Ariber'. Simcha Engel turns up with a shoe missing: he danced so hard he lost it, after hearing the Rebbe's teaching that joyful dancing now can make up for whatever was missed earlier in the season. Rabbi Goldstein lists the Ushpizin and explains that tonight's guests, Yosef HaTzaddik and the Rebbe Maharash, teach that a Jew can leap straight to the greatest heights, just as Yosef went from prison to ruler at once. He then begins a story of a Jewish innkeeper whose village priest wants to drive him out of business. The story pauses while groups of children recite the Twelve Pesukim and Al Tira. When it resumes, the priest pretends to make peace, swaps in a poisoned bottle, and blames the innkeeper when a customer dies. The Rebbe Maharash puts off seeing him for two days, then sends him straight home on a first-class train ticket, where he unknowingly pours out his heart to the very judges of his case. They uncover the priest's plot and the innkeeper goes free.
display.lesson: Listen to the Rebbe even when we do not understand; the Rebbe's words are true. And a Jew can leap to great heights at once, Lechatchila Ariber.

date.note: 'Tonight the leader is Yosef HaTzaddik and the Rebbe Maharash' = sixth night of Sukkos (Motzaei Shabbos, 11 Oct 2025); year from the 5786 series.

advisories.note: A customer drinks poisoned liquor and dies as part of the priest's plot.
A priest schemes against a Jewish innkeeper and has him falsely accused of murder; he is cleared.
The story is set in an inn; the priest gets drunk and reveals his plot.

quality.notes: Live rally with loud drums. ASR repetition loops at about 7:02 and 17:57. The innkeeper's name is garbled (Akiva / Yechiel / Yankel). 'Maharaj' = Maharash.
